blocks.passage:
Remote communication has its own grammar. On a video call, you cannot simply start speaking when you feel ready — you might cut across someone else because of a delay, or miss your moment entirely because everyone is being too polite.

Good video participants signal before they speak. A small wave, a short "can I add something?", or simply using the chat for quick points. They also use people's names more than in person, because eye contact doesn't travel through a screen.

Audio quality matters more than people think. A cheap headset makes you harder to follow, which quietly undermines everything you say. Investing in a decent microphone is one of the smallest, most effective professional moves you can make.

items.q: Why can't you just start speaking when ready on a video call?
options: A delay may make you cut across someone, or over-politeness makes you miss your turn
The host must call your name
items.why: "you might cut across someone else because of a delay, or miss your moment entirely because everyone is being too polite."

items.q: What do good video participants do before they speak?
options: Signal — a wave, a short phrase, or the chat
items.why: "Good video participants signal before they speak."

items.q: Why do they use people's names more than in person?
options: Because eye contact doesn't travel through a screen
items.why: "because eye contact doesn't travel through a screen."

items.q: What effect does a cheap headset have, according to the text?
options: It saves money with no downside
It quietly undermines everything you say
items.why: "A cheap headset makes you harder to follow, which quietly undermines everything you say."

items.q: The author calls a decent microphone "one of the smallest, most effective professional moves" because it…
options: gives a large benefit for a small effort
items.why: Inferência: pequeno investimento, grande efeito na forma como você é ouvido.

audio.text:
We're twelve people on this call, so let me set a couple of ground rules before we start, otherwise we'll all talk over each other.

If you want to speak, use the raise-hand button or just drop a note in the chat and I'll bring you in. Please don't jump straight in — with the lag, two people starting at once is painful for everyone.

Keep yourselves on mute when you're not talking. There's a lot of background noise from open offices today, and it makes the speaker really hard to follow.

Emily, I can see your hand is up — go ahead, the floor's yours.

Thanks. When you've made your point, please hand back clearly, something like "that's me, back to you", so I know the turn is finished and I can move to the next person.

items.q: Why does the host set ground rules first?
options: Because with twelve people they'll talk over each other otherwise
items.why: "twelve people… otherwise we'll all talk over each other."

items.q: How should participants signal that they want to speak?
options: Raise-hand button or a note in the chat
items.why: "use the raise-hand button or just drop a note in the chat and I'll bring you in."

items.q: Why does the host ask people not to "jump straight in"?
options: With the lag, two people starting at once is painful
items.why: "with the lag, two people starting at once is painful for everyone."

items.q: Why does the host ask everyone to stay on mute?
options: Because background noise makes the speaker hard to follow
items.why: "a lot of background noise… makes the speaker really hard to follow."

items.q: Why does the host want people to "hand back clearly"?
options: So the host knows the turn is finished and can move on
items.why: "so I know the turn is finished and I can move to the next person."

items.q: "There's a bit of **lag** on the line, so give it a second." Lag means…
items.why: Lag = atraso na transmissão.

items.q: "Please stay on **mute** unless you're speaking." To be on mute means…
options: your microphone is off to others
items.why: Mute = mudo; o microfone não é ouvido pelos outros.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "There's too much ___ — can everyone mute?"
items.why: Background noise = ruído de fundo.

items.q: **Turn-taking** on a call refers to…
options: the orderly way people take turns to speak
items.why: Turn-taking = alternância organizada de quem fala.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I'll **hand over** to Emily now for the numbers." To hand over means to…
items.why: Hand over = passar a palavra.

items.q: "Can I **add something** here?" This phrase is used to…
items.why: Um sinal educado de que você quer contribuir.

items.q: "Sorry, you're **breaking up** — could you repeat that?" To break up means…
options: the audio is cutting in and out
items.why: Break up (numa chamada) = o áudio está cortando.

items.q: "You're on **mute** — we can't hear you." This tells someone to…
items.why: Aviso clássico: a pessoa fala mas está no mudo.

items.q: "Let me **jump in** quickly before we move on." To jump in means to…
items.why: Jump in = entrar rapidamente na conversa.

items.q: "Let's **take this offline** and sort it after the call." To take something offline means to…
options: discuss it separately, outside this meeting
items.why: Take offline = tratar em separado, fora da reunião atual.
